incompatibilities.effect: Combined use increases irritation, redness, and peeling. Both exfoliate — using them together strips the skin barrier faster than it can repair.
incompatibilities.recommendation: Use on alternate days or at different times (retinoid at night, AHA in the morning).

incompatibilities.effect: Benzoyl peroxide oxidizes and deactivates retinoids on contact, making both less effective.
incompatibilities.recommendation: Apply at different times of day.
incompatibilities.source: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology

incompatibilities.effect: At high concentrations, these can reduce each other's efficacy and cause flushing. At typical cosmetic concentrations the interaction is mild.
incompatibilities.recommendation: Generally fine together in modern formulations. If you experience flushing, apply at different times.

incompatibilities.effect: Both are acidic. Layering them can drop skin pH too low, causing irritation and compromising the skin barrier.
incompatibilities.recommendation: Use at different times of day.

incompatibilities.effect: Both cause dryness and exfoliation. Combined use increases risk of irritation, peeling, and barrier damage.

known_irritants.effect: Fragrance is the most common cause of cosmetic contact dermatitis. Repeated exposure can develop into sensitivity over time.
Strong surfactant that strips natural oils and disrupts the skin barrier. Common cause of dryness and irritation, especially in eczema-prone skin.
known_irritants.source: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology

known_irritants.effect: Dries skin and damages the moisture barrier with repeated use. Fatty alcohols (cetyl, cetearyl) are different and are not irritants.
